```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```


```{r}
healthcare_dataset = read.csv("healthcare_dataset.csv")

```

## 1. Print the Structure of the dataset

```{r}
str(healthcare_dataset)
```
## 2. List the variables in the dataset
```{r}
names(healthcare_dataset)
```
## 3. Print the top 15 rows of the dataset
```{r}
head(healthcare_dataset,15)
```
## 4. Write a user defined function using a variable in the dataset
```{r}
average_age = function(age)(mean(age, na.rm = TRUE))
average_age(healthcare_dataset$Age)
```
## 5. Use data manipulation techniques and filter rows based on any logical criteria that exist in the dataset
```{r}
filtered_healthcare = subset(healthcare_dataset, Age >60 & Billing.Amount >30000,select = c(Name, Age, Medical.Condition, Billing.Amount))
head(filtered_healthcare,15)
```

## 6. Identify the dependent and independent variables and use reshaping techniques and create a new data frame by joining those variables from your dataset
```{r}
independent = healthcare_dataset[, c("Name", "Age", "Medical.Condition")]
dependent = healthcare_dataset[, c("Name", "Age", "Billing.Amount")]
joined_healthcare = merge(independent, dependent, by ="Name")
head(joined_healthcare,15)
```

## 7. Remove missing values in the dataset
```{r}
sum(is.na(healthcare_dataset))
```
#Clean healthcare dateset
```{r}
clean_healthcare = na.omit(healthcare_dataset)
```
## 8. Identify and remove duplicated data in the dataset
```{r}
sum(duplicated(healthcare_dataset))
```
#Remove duplicate data
```{r}
healthcare_unique = unique(healthcare_dataset)
```

#check if the duplicates have been removed
```{r}
sum(duplicated(healthcare_unique))
```
## 9. Reorder multiple rows in descending order
```{r}
sorted_healthcare = healthcare_unique[order(-healthcare_unique$Age,-healthcare_unique$Billing.Amount),]
head(sorted_healthcare,15)
```

## 10. Rename some of the column names in the dataset
```{r}
colnames(healthcare_dataset)
```
#Rename
```{r}
renamed_healthcare = sorted_healthcare
names(renamed_healthcare)[2] = "Patient_Age"
names(renamed_healthcare)[5] = "Diagnosis"
names(renamed_healthcare)[10] = "Medical_Bill"
head(renamed_healthcare,15)
```

## 11.	Add new variables in your data frame by using a mathematical function (for e.g. – multiply an existing column by 2 and add it as a new variable to your data frame
```{r}
renamed_healthcare$Double_Bill = renamed_healthcare$Medical_Bill * 2
head(renamed_healthcare[, c("Medical_Bill", "Double_Bill")], 15)
```

## 12.	Create a training set using random number generator engine.
```{r}
library(dplyr)
set.seed(1234)
Training_healthcare = renamed_healthcare %>% sample_frac(0.80, rep = FALSE)
Training_healthcare = as.data.frame(Training_healthcare)
head(Training_healthcare, 15)
```

## 12.	Print the summary statistics of the dataset.
```{r}
summary(Training_healthcare)
```

## 13.	Use any of the numerical variables from the dataset and perform the following statistical functions(Mean, Median, Mode,Range.

#mean
```{r}
mean(Training_healthcare$Patient_Age)
```
#median
```{r}
median(Training_healthcare$Patient_Age)
```
#mode
```{r}
Age_frequency = table(Training_healthcare$Patient_Age)
names(Age_frequency)[which.max(Age_frequency)]
```
#Range
```{r}
range(Training_healthcare$Patient_Age)
```

## 14.	Plot a scatter plot for any 2 variables in the dataset.
```{r}
ggplot(data = Training_healthcare, aes(x= Patient_Age, y= Medical_Bill)) + geom_point(color = "palegreen")
```

## 15.	Plot a bar plot for any 2 variables in the dataset.
```{r}
ggplot(data = Training_healthcare, aes(x= Diagnosis)) + geom_bar(color = "palegreen4")
```

## 16.	Find the correlation between any 2 variables in the dataset by applying Pearson correlation.
```{r}
cor(Training_healthcare$Patient_Age,Training_healthcare$Medical_Bill,method = "pearson")
```
